codes.rationale: Acute bilateral lobar/segmental PE without acute cor pulmonale (provider documented, normal RV) is the condition chiefly responsible for admission.
codes.critic_reason: Provider-documented acute bilateral PE without acute cor pulmonale, consistent across H&P, progress note and discharge summary. Treated with heparin then apixaban. Lobar/segmental location does not change the code; no saddle PE documented.
codes.description: Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale

codes.rationale: Provider documents acute hypoxic respiratory failure due to PE, with SpO2 82% RA and NRB requirement, which is not integral to PE.
codes.critic_reason: Provider documents acute hypoxic respiratory failure due to PE through the discharge summary. Clinical indicators are strong: SpO2 82% RA, RR 28, work of breathing, NRB/15L need, PaO2 68 on NRB. Resolved by discharge, which is consistent.

codes.rationale: CAD documented as a chronic condition and treated with continued meds, with no angina.
codes.critic_reason: CAD is documented by the provider in H&P and discharge summary and is managed with aspirin, statin and beta-blocker. No angina is documented. Coronary calcification on radiology is not needed as support.
codes.description: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris

codes.rationale: Status post PCI with DES to LAD.
codes.critic_reason: Provider documents s/p PCI with DES to LAD in H&P and discharge summary.
codes.description: Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft

codes.rationale: Hypertension is documented and treated, with no heart or kidney involvement documented.
codes.critic_reason: HTN is documented and treated (metoprolol, lisinopril). No CKD or heart failure is documented, so I10 is appropriate. Cr is 1.1 with no CKD diagnosis.

codes.rationale: Hyperlipidemia is treated with a statin.
codes.critic_reason: Hyperlipidemia is documented by the provider and treated with atorvastatin.

codes.rationale: T2DM is documented, but the provider did not document hyperglycemia, so the code is without complications.
codes.critic_reason: Provider documents T2DM on insulin with no documented complication. Glucose 212 is a lab value only and is not a provider diagnosis. E11.9 is correct unless a query yields hyperglycemia.
Provider documents insulin-requiring T2DM with glargine at home and at discharge.

codes.rationale: Metformin is on the home and discharge medication lists, and guidelines say to code oral hypoglycemic use together with insulin.
codes.critic_reason: Metformin is on the home and discharge medication lists, so Z79.84 is reportable. OCG I.C.4.a.3 says to assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84 when a patient takes insulin and an oral hypoglycemic. Metformin was held inpatient but resumed at discharge, so this is chronic use.
codes.description: Long term (current) use of oral hypoglycemic drugs

codes.rationale: Daily aspirin 81 mg is a long-term medication.
codes.critic_reason: Aspirin 81 mg is a home medication and is continued at discharge. A provider note says cardiology will reassess its need with the DOAC. Chronic use is documented, so the code is valid.

codes.rationale: The patient is a former smoker who quit in 2019.
codes.critic_reason: Provider documents former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2019, with no current tobacco use.

issues.summary: CTA read 'may reflect early infarct' for the RLL wedge opacity. Radiology alone is not codable, so query the provider about pulmonary infarction. If confirmed, I26.99 would still apply, since infarction is included in the PE code.
Glucose was 212 in a patient with T2DM, but no provider documented hyperglycemia. Query if clinically significant.

The troponin leak was attributed to PE strain physiology. No myocardial injury diagnosis was documented, and cor pulmonale was explicitly negated, so none was coded. Consider a query only if myocardial injury is clinically intended.

Z79.01 for long-term anticoagulant (apixaban) was not proposed. Apixaban is a new start for the acute PE with a planned duration decision by hematology, so it is likely not reportable as long-term use at this time. Confirm intent per facility policy.
The H&P states glargine 18 u in the plan while the home medication list says 24 u. This is a minor dosing discrepancy and does not affect coding.
